findings.rationale: BMI and PhysHlth distributions are far outside the federation: BMI mean is ~20.6 (median client ~28.9) with a 1st percentile near 0 and sd inflated to 12.4 (median sd ~6.4), consistent with a sentinel code (0) in roughly a quarter of records. PhysHlth has a 99th percentile around 73 and mean ~22.5 (median mean ~4.6), consistent with sentinel values in about a fifth of records. The same pattern is already present at round 1, so the fault starts at round 1, and it is not a drift. Its updates are also anomalous (min cosine -0.63, strongly flagged), which is what training on corrupted features would produce.

Same sentinel signature as HI: BMI 1st percentile about -0.07 with mean 21.45 and inflated sd 14.3 (z_noise -15.1), and PhysHlth 99th percentile 73.7 with mean 22.2 (z_noise 35.2). Round-1 values are already abnormal, so the fault is present from round 1. Updates are anomalous (min cosine -0.55, median norm ratio 1.84).

Same sentinel signature: BMI 1st percentile about 0.27 with mean 22.3 and sd 14.5 (z_noise -12.8), and PhysHlth 99th percentile 72.9 with mean 22.5 (z_noise 27.6). Round-1 values already show the artefact, so the fault starts at round 1. Updates are anomalous (min cosine -0.51, median norm ratio 1.75, z=+3.1). Its AgeGroup-5 subgroup O/E is also extreme, which is consistent with corrupted features driving predictions.

Low-confidence lead. GU has the lowest mean update cosine among the non-artefact clients (about 0.15 over 20 rounds, against a federation typically around 0.5), and its median norm ratio is elevated for its small size (z=+3.8). Its per-round cosines swing between about -1 and +1 across two independent pulls, which is the jitter that random-noise uploads would produce. Its local AUC (0.83) and calibration are normal, consistent with 'accuracy barely moves'. Evidence is weak: the per-round values are very noisy and the size is small (n=708), so this is not confirmed.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then confirmed with narrower queries. Three clients (HI, MD, TX) show a clear, consistent missing-value artefact: sentinel-like tails in BMI and PhysHlth, present from round 1, with anomalous updates. I classed these as missing_artefact with onset round 1. Their local performance is normal, so this is not label noise or prevalence shift. GU is a weak lead for explanation_instability (low mean cosine, elevated norm for its size, erratic per-round updates), reported at low confidence (0.4). Other candidates were not supported: AL's Stroke shift is a one-off spike and not a persistent drift; no client shows the low O/E pattern of subgroup under-diagnosis; no client has a CITL or AUC flag, so no label-noise or prevalence-shift evidence; and no client shows the persistent update anomaly that poisoning would produce. The remaining budget was fully spent (0.0 left).
